title: Intake vacuum leak smoke test
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. With the engine off, introduce smoke into the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the intake manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke. A lean code that is worst at idle and improves above 2,000 rpm usually indicates unmetered air entering after the airflow sensor.
step: With the engine off, smoke-test the intake through the brake booster vacuum line and watch the manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, PCV hoses and vacuum lines for escaping smoke
results: A shop smoke-tested the intake for me. No smoke came out anywhere.
The smoke test was clean, nothing leaking at the manifold, throttle body or hoses.

title: Fuel pressure and hold test, returnless systems
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines with a fuel rail test port. Key on, engine off, connect a pressure gauge at the rail test port. Specified pressure is 55-62 psi, and it should hold within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off. Low pressure can produce lean codes and a rough idle; low pressure together with high fuel trims at all speeds points to fuel delivery.
step: Key on, engine off, connect a gauge at the fuel rail test port and confirm 55-62 psi that holds within 5 psi for 5 minutes after key-off
results: Borrowed a gauge. It read 58 psi and held for the full five minutes.
Fuel pressure was 60 psi key on and barely dropped after I shut it off.

title: Coolant temperature sensor plausibility check
text: On 2010-2015 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

results: Scan tool said 201 and the infrared gun said 196 at the housing.
Coolant temp on the scanner and the IR reading were within a few degrees of each other.

text: On 2016-2021 models, with the engine fully warm, compare the engine coolant temperature (ECT) reading on a scan tool with an infrared thermometer reading taken at the thermostat housing. The two should agree within 10 deg F. A sensor that reads cold on a hot engine makes the control module add extra fuel on restart, which can flood a hot engine.

title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. A strong blue spark should jump the gap on every crank. A weak, orange or intermittent spark indicates the coil cannot supply enough voltage under load.
step: Connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV to the coil from the misfiring cylinder and crank with fuel disabled, watching for a strong blue spark on every crank
results: Hooked up a spark tester at 25 kV. Strong blue spark every time.
The spark tester showed a solid blue spark the whole time I cranked it.

title: Spark output test with an adjustable spark tester
text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines with individual coil-on-plug ignition. Remove the coil from the misfiring cylinder, connect an adjustable spark tester set to 25 kV between the coil and engine ground, and crank with fuel disabled. title: Cranking compression test
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.
step: With fuel and ignition disabled and the throttle held open, run a cranking compression test and compare the misfiring cylinder with the rest
results: Compression was 175 to 180 on every cylinder, including the one with the code.
All cylinders came in within a few psi of each other on compression.

title: Cranking compression test
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. Disable fuel and ignition, remove all spark plugs and crank each cylinder through at least five compression strokes with the throttle held open. All cylinders should read within 10 percent of each other. A cylinder that reads low points to a mechanical cause rather than an ignition or fuel cause.

title: Coolant level and trapped air check
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2015. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. Never open the cap on a hot engine. Low coolant, or air trapped near the thermostat housing, causes temperature to swing upward at idle while airflow at speed can mask it.
step: With the engine cold, open the radiator or degas bottle cap and look at whether coolant is right up to the neck or the cold-fill line
results: Checked it cold this morning. Coolant is right up to the neck.
Level is at the cold-fill line, nothing low.

text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2016-2021. With the engine cold, remove the radiator cap or degas bottle cap and check that coolant is at the neck or the cold-fill line. title: Cooling system pressure test
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.
step: With the engine cold, pressurize the cooling system to the cap rating and watch for a pressure drop over 15 minutes while you inspect the hoses, water pump weep hole and radiator tanks
results: Pressure-tested it cold. Held steady for 15 minutes and nothing dripped.
It held 16 psi for fifteen minutes with no wet spots anywhere.

title: Cooling system pressure test
text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 5.5L V8 engines. With the engine cold, fit a cooling system pressure tester to the radiator neck or reservoir and pump to the pressure stamped on the cap. Pressure should hold for 15 minutes. While the system is pressurized, inspect the hoses, the heater hoses at the firewall, the water pump weep hole and the radiator end tanks for seepage.

title: Combustion leak (block) test
text: On 2016-2021 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. Blue fluid that turns yellow or green indicates combustion gases in the coolant. Keep the test fluid out of the coolant itself, and use fresh fluid for each test. A tester with a squeeze bulb makes the draw easier.
step: With the engine warm and idling, run a combustion leak test by drawing air from above the coolant through the tester fluid and watching for a color change
results: Ran the block tester. The fluid stayed blue the whole time.
Combustion leak test showed no color change at all.

title: Combustion leak (block) test
text: On 2010-2015 models, with the engine warm and idling, remove the reservoir cap and use a combustion leak tester to draw air from above the coolant through the test fluid. title: Heater core inlet and outlet temperature check
text: Valid for 2010-2015 models. With the engine at operating temperature, the heat set to full hot and the blower on high, measure both heater hoses at the firewall with an infrared thermometer. Both hoses should be hot and within about 15 deg F of each other. A cool outlet hose with a hot inlet indicates restricted flow through the heater core.
step: With the engine at operating temperature and the heat on full, measure both heater hoses at the firewall with an infrared thermometer and compare them
results: Both heater hoses are hot, 182 and 174.
Inlet and outlet heater hoses were within about ten degrees, both hot to the touch.

title: Heater core inlet and outlet temperature check
text: Valid for 2016-2021 models. With the engine at operating temperature, the heat set to full hot and the blower on high, measure both heater hoses at the firewall with an infrared thermometer. Both hoses should be hot and within about 15 deg F of each other. A cool outlet hose with a hot inlet indicates restricted flow through the heater core.

title: Coolant level check for low heater output
text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines. In many cooling systems the heater core sits at the highest point, so it is the first part of the system to lose flow when coolant is low. With the engine cold, check the level at the radiator neck or degas bottle rather than relying on the overflow tank mark. A flashlight behind an opaque bottle makes the level easier to see.
step: With the engine cold, check the coolant level at the radiator neck or degas bottle rather than the overflow tank
results: Coolant is full at the radiator neck.
Checked at the degas bottle cold and it's right at the line.

title: Coolant level check for low heater output

title: Battery state-of-health test
text: Applies to compact sedans, minivans and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2020. Fully charge the battery and let it rest for at least one hour. Resting voltage should be 12.6 V or higher. Run a conductance or load test and compare the result with the cold cranking amps (CCA) rating on the label. A battery below about 70 percent of its rating cannot hold enough charge to survive several days parked. Clean the posts before testing.
step: Fully charge the battery, let it rest, and run a conductance or load test against the CCA rating on its label
results: Charged it overnight and the tester says 680 CCA against a 700 rating. It passed.
Resting voltage was 12.7 and it passed the load test.

title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat after several days parked even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.
step: After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V
results: After the drive it showed 14.2 V at the battery with the lights and blower on.
Charging voltage was 13.9 volts at 2,000 rpm.

title: Recharge check for repeat dead batteries
text: A battery that is not brought back to full charge during normal driving goes flat overnight in freezing air even with no excess draw. After a 20 minute drive, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights and blower on, measure voltage at the battery posts. A reading of 13.5-14.7 V shows the charging system is recharging the battery. Measure at the posts, not the cable clamps.

title: Charging voltage test under load
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.
step: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts and compare it with 13.5-14.7 V
results: 14.1 volts at the battery with everything on.
The meter showed 13.9 V at 2,000 rpm with all the loads on.

title: Charging voltage test under load
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. With the engine at 2,000 rpm and the headlights, blower on high and rear defrost on, measure voltage across the battery posts with a digital meter. Expect 13.5-14.7 V. A reading below 13.0 V with loads on indicates low charging output. Clean any corrosion from the posts first so it does not skew the reading.

title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
text: On 2016-2021 models, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side. Probe the terminals themselves, not the cable clamps, so a loose clamp shows up.
step: With the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy loads on, measure voltage drop between the alternator output terminal and the battery positive post, and between the alternator case and the battery negative post
results: 0.1 V drop on the positive side and 0.05 on the ground side.
Voltage drop across both charging cables, positive and ground, was tiny, under a tenth of a volt.

title: Charging circuit voltage drop test
text: On 2010-2015 models, with the engine at 2,000 rpm and heavy electrical loads on, measure voltage drop from the alternator output terminal to the battery positive post, and from the alternator case to the battery negative post. Drop should be under 0.3 V on the positive side and under 0.2 V on the ground side. Probe the terminals themselves, not the cable clamps, so a loose clamp shows up.

title: Starter circuit voltage drop test
text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines. With a helper holding the ignition in the start position, measure voltage drop from the battery positive post to the starter B+ terminal, and from the battery negative post to the engine block. Each side should be under 0.5 V. A higher drop means the starter cannot draw enough current to turn the engine, even when the battery is charged.
step: With a helper holding the key in start, measure voltage drop from the battery positive post to the starter B+ terminal and from the battery negative post to the engine block; each side should be under 0.5 V
results: Positive side drop was 0.2 V while it clicked, and the ground side was 0.1 V.
Measured 0.3 volts on the positive cable and 0.1 on the ground cable during the start attempt.

title: Starter circuit voltage drop test
text: Applies to 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 5.5L V8 engines. title: Battery voltage during a start attempt
text: Covers 2009-2022 models. Connect a meter across the battery posts and watch the reading while a helper attempts to start the engine. Voltage should not fall below 9.6 V. A battery that collapses below that value cannot power the starter even if dash lights look bright with the key on. Keep clear of the fan and belt during the attempt.

title: Rotor thickness variation
text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes, model years 2010-2015. Using an outside micrometer, measure rotor thickness at eight evenly spaced points about 0.5 in from the outer edge. Thickness variation must not exceed 0.0005 in. Variation above this limit produces pedal pulsation during braking from speed. Clean rust scale off the measuring track first.

results: Thickness variation was 0.0003 inch on both rotors.
Micrometer readings varied by less than half a thousandth around each rotor.

title: Rotor thickness variation

title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and an automatic transmission. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

results: Rotor faces look even all the way around, no dark patches or hard spots.

title: Rotor surface inspection for uneven pad transfer
text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes and a manual-clutch transaxle. Remove the front wheels and inspect both faces of each rotor in good light. Dark, blotchy patches of pad material, or blue-gray hard spots that a file skates over, indicate uneven pad transfer or hard spots that grab the pad once per revolution and are felt as pulsation when braking from speed.

title: Brake temperature comparison
text: Applies to 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines. After a test drive with several moderate stops, park without using the parking brake and measure each front rotor face with an infrared thermometer. Temperatures should be within about 50 deg F side to side. A large difference shows which side is braking harder or dragging. Take both readings within a minute of stopping.

title: Brake temperature comparison

title: Front tire match and pressure check
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2015. Check that both front tires are the same size, brand, model and approximate tread depth, and set cold pressures to the door placard. A mismatched tire, or a large pressure difference side to side, can cause a pull that is most noticeable under braking. Look for uneven wear across each tread as well.

results: Both fronts are the same brand and size, about the same tread, and 35 psi each.

text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. Check that both front tires are the same size, brand, model and approximate tread depth, and set cold pressures to the door placard. title: Stabilizer link inspection
text: Applies to vehicles with a front stabilizer bar, model years 2010-2015. With the vehicle on the ground so the suspension is loaded, grasp each stabilizer link and push and pull firmly. Watch both ball studs for play or a knock. Any free play, or a torn boot with grease loss, indicates a worn link. A short pry bar helps on stiff links.

title: Lower ball joint play check
text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans and hatchbacks. Raise the vehicle with a jack under the lower control arm so the ball joint is loaded, and support it on a stand. Place a pry bar under the tire and lift while watching the joint between the knuckle and control arm. Specification is zero measurable vertical play. A helper can watch the joint while you lift.

results: No movement at the lower ball joints with the pry bar.

title: Tire radial runout check
text: Applies to vehicles with automatic or CVT transmissions, model years 2009-2022. With the vehicle raised, set a dial indicator against the center tread rib and rotate each tire one full turn. Radial runout should not exceed 0.060 in. A higher reading indicates an out-of-round tire or a bent wheel. Drive a few miles first so flat spots from parking do not skew the reading.
step: With the vehicle raised, set a dial indicator on the center tread rib to measure radial runout of each tire against the 0.060 in limit

title: Tire tread and belt inspection
text: On 2010-2015 models, with the vehicle raised, slowly rotate each tire and run a gloved hand across the tread and sidewalls. Feel for lumps, a wavy tread line or cupping, which indicate a shifted belt or separation. Look for a tread rib that wanders as the tire turns. Check the inner shoulder too, where damage is easy to miss.

results: No lumps or cupping on any of them.

title: Brake fluid level and leak inspection
text: Covers 2016-2021 models. Check the master cylinder reservoir level against the MIN and MAX marks. Inspect each caliper, wheel cylinder, brake hose and steel line for wetness, and check the joint between the master cylinder and the brake booster for fluid seepage from the rear seal. Wipe suspect areas clean so fresh seepage is easy to spot.
step: Look at the reservoir level against its marks and at each caliper, hose, line and the master cylinder-to-booster joint for fluid wetness
results: Reservoir is at MAX and there are no wet spots at any wheel or at the master cylinder.
Fluid level is fine and everything looks dry.

title: Brake fluid level and leak inspection
text: Covers 2010-2015 models. Check the master cylinder reservoir level against the MIN and MAX marks. Inspect each caliper, wheel cylinder, brake hose and steel line for wetness, and check the joint between the master cylinder and the brake booster for fluid seepage from the rear seal. title: Brake fluid moisture test
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2020. Test the fluid in the reservoir with a brake fluid tester or test strip. Fluid with more than 3 percent water has a reduced boiling point and can vaporize in the calipers, producing a soft pedal. Fluid that is dark or cloudy also indicates contamination. Take the sample before any fluid is added.
step: Test the fluid in the reservoir with a brake fluid tester or test strip and compare its water content with the 3 percent limit
results: The tester shows about 1 percent moisture.
Test strip came back in the good range, fluid looks clear.

title: Brake fluid moisture test
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2010-2020. Test the fluid in the reservoir with a brake fluid tester or test strip. Fluid with more than 3 percent water has a reduced boiling point and can vaporize after hot stops, producing a soft pedal. Fluid that is dark or cloudy also indicates contamination. Take the sample before any fluid is added.

title: Compressor clutch engagement check
text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor, model years 2016-2021. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.
step: With the engine running, the AC on max and the blower on high, watch whether the compressor clutch plate pulls in and spins with the pulley
results: The clutch pulls in and stays engaged, spinning with the pulley.

title: Compressor clutch engagement check
text: Applies to models with a clutch-driven compressor, model years 2010-2015. With the engine running, the AC at maximum and the blower on high, watch the compressor front plate. The plate should pull in and spin with the pulley. A plate that stays still, or cycles on and off every few moments, points to the clutch circuit or a low refrigerant charge.

title: AC operating pressure check
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines, model years 2010-2022. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

results: Low side was 38 and high side 210 at about 85 degrees out.
Gauges read right in the normal range for the outside temperature.

title: AC operating pressure check
text: Applies to 1.8L I4, 2.4L I4 and 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2010-2022. Connect a manifold gauge set to the service ports. With the engine at 1,500 rpm, the AC at maximum and doors open, compare readings with the chart for the ambient temperature. At about 80 deg F, typical readings are 25-45 psi on the low side and 150-250 psi on the high side. Wear eye protection at the ports.

title: Automatic transmission fluid level and condition
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2011-2021. With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

results: Fluid is at the hot full mark, red, with no burnt smell.

title: CVT fluid level and condition
text: Applies to vehicles with a continuously-variable (CVT) gearbox, model years 2011-2021. With the fluid at operating temperature, the engine idling in park and the vehicle level, check the fluid level against the hot range. Fluid should be red or pink with no burnt odor or debris. Low or degraded fluid causes delayed and harsh shifts.

title: Engine and transmission mount check
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2016-2021. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.
step: With the brake held firmly, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine for lift or a gap at any mount
results: The engine barely moves when shifting and the mounts look intact.
No real lift at all going between drive and reverse.

title: Engine and transmission mount check
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission, model years 2010-2015. With the hood open, the brake held firmly and the engine idling, have a helper shift between drive and reverse while you watch the engine. Lift of more than about 0.5 in, or a visible gap at a mount, indicates a broken mount that can make normal shifts feel harsh.
